newsitem.title: USA: Due to queries, USDA checks Japan corn sales data. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT 31/5]
newsitem.headline: Due to queries, USDA checks Japan corn sales data. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT 31/5]

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said it was standing by its report of 562,700 tonnes of U.S. corn were sold to Japan in the week ending May 22 for 1996/97 (corrects year from "1997/98") delivery but it also was double-checking with exporters.
The Japan sales, listed in USDA's weekly export sales report, amounted to half of the 1,002,900 tonnes of old-crop corn sold in the week, a sharply higher total than normal.
"We stick by that number," a USDA official said. "What we've got in there is what's been reported to us."
Due to queries, the official said, USDA was contacting exporters to verify shipping dates and, thus, sales years.
There were rumors in the Chicago grain markets that some of the corn sold to Japan actually was for 1997/98 delivery. It was unclear how much corn might be involved.
"It is a concern. We are aware of it," the official said.
If some sales were attributed to the wrong year, USDA will identify the change in next week's report, he said.

This week's report showed 216,300 tonnes of outstanding sales of U.S. new-crop corn to Japan. One year ago, the new-crop figure was 2,716,100 tonnes. A year before that, about 1.4 million tonnes of new-crop corn had been sold to Japan.

USDA reported 3,323,700 tonnes of outstanding corn sales and 11,140,600 tonnes of exports to Japan in 1996/97 through May 22. The comparable figures at this point in 1995/96 were 4,642,600 tonnes of outstanding sales and 11,781,100 tonnes of accumulated exports.
